classification.difficultyReason: Apply simultaneous horizontal and vertical dilations to a supplied graph.

spec.description: Unfilled cubic-shaped illustrative curve, with a maximum left of the vertical axis, a minimum right of it, three horizontal-axis crossings including the origin, and downward-left and upward-right tails.
spec.mathematics: The function rule and turning-point coordinates are unspecified. Bézier controls reproduce qualitative topology only. The nearby source labels −2 and 2 are retained without asserting exact intercept coordinates.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent supplied graph; no transformed curve appears in the student prompt.

answer.short: Dilate horizontally by a factor of $\frac12$ and vertically by a factor of $\frac12$. Each point $(u,v)$ becomes $\left(\frac u2,\frac v2\right)$; the origin stays fixed.
answer.worked:
Replacing $x$ by $2x$ halves horizontal distances from the $y$-axis. Multiplying the function by $\frac12$ halves vertical distances from the $x$-axis.
$$\begin{align*}x_{\mathrm{new}}&=\frac{x_{\mathrm{old}}}{2}\\y_{\mathrm{new}}&=\frac{y_{\mathrm{old}}}{2}\end{align*}$$
Sketch the same shape with both distances halved, retaining the origin and the directions of the tails.
